state.lastRunNotes: Fourth consecutive down session, but today's move is a sharp acceleration of the same macro story: rising bond yields (US 10Y ~4.79%, AU long bond back to 2011 levels) are compressing multiples on long-duration growth names (XRO -32%, WTC -27%, CAR -21.5%, MIN -21.6%, PLS -27.3%), not company-specific news. Volume stays well below average (vol_x 0.2-0.56) across the board, so there's no capitulation signal, just a broad derating. Held PME fell -15.85% with zero negative company news -- Buy consensus and $202.77 target intact, still above its A$150 stop. CBA's -4.91% also has no bank-specific news behind it (broad premium-valuation compression, not the NSW contract thesis breaking) and TLS is flat/up. No genuine specific catalyst on any watchlist name, so holding across the board rather than reacting to macro-driven volatility.

trades.horizon: Hold through next quarterly update; reassess if NSW contract synergies fail to show in FY27 guidance or valuation stretches materially above sector average P/E.
trades.rationale: Won NSW state government banking services contract (liquidity management, transaction banking, FX, transit payments) — durable revenue catalyst for defensive core bank holding.
trades.sentimentSummary: Neutral-to-positive — contract win noted amid general bank sector softness today.
